body: [{"streamId":"01a0de47-5a22-761f-a173-e2e4726ebd91","eventTypeName":"Hall9k.Domain.Features.Tasks.Events.TaskAdded","eventDataJson":"{\u0022Id\u0022:\u002201a0de47-5a22-761f-a173-e2e4726ebd91\u0022,\u0022ProjectId\u0022:\u002201a0a27f-abdf-7731-84aa-d604e9bc53ca\u0022,\u0022Objective\u0022:\u0022A repeat odo walk opens a detail page only for a posting the ledger has never seen, and records a search card whose link is already on the ledger from the card alone (still listed, current price), so price drops and Gone keep coming from the search pages while detail visits go only to new cars\u0022,\u0022AcceptanceCriteria\u0022:[\u0022The walk\\u0027s search-page pull returns, for every detail link, the text of that link\\u0027s own result card (the nearest ancestor element of the anchor whose text contains a dollar amount, with a per-site container override allowed), and the recorder writes the links with their card text beside search.txt (for example cards.json) so fixtures can be cut later; search.txt itself is unchanged; proven by a test over a fake page whose anchors sit inside card elements\u0022,\u0022WalkSite gains a card price reader that returns the card\\u0027s asking price (the first dollar amount in the card text, null when none) for cars.com and carvana, proven by tests over card texts cut from the recorded 2026-09-26 search pages (cars.com: a card reads price, then mileage, then a Used \\u003Cyear\\u003E title; carvana: \\u0027Current price:\\u0027 then the amount); autotrader gets the same reader once its card shape is confirmed from a recorded page, or a documented null until then\u0022,\u0022Before visiting a pair\\u0027s detail links, the walk touches every canonical link already on the ledger for that source through a new LedgerUpsertService method (find the posting by Source and Url; stamp LastSeen with the run\\u0027s own StartedAt; append a PriceObservation when the card price is known and differs from the latest; keep the dealer, shipping fee, and vehicle row as they are); touched links leave the detail pool and never spend the cap; a known link whose card price could not be read is still touched without a price observation; a new flag, --revisit, forces detail visits for every link as today; proven by tests: a seeded posting seen again at a lower card price yields a Price drop and no Gone, and one absent from the cards yields Gone\u0022,\u0022The per-pair summary line and the end-of-run table gain a known-from-cards count beside visited, saved, and dropped; the README\\u0027s walk section (or docs/walk.md if the docs split has landed) explains that a repeat walk visits only new cars and how --revisit changes that; dotnet build and dotnet test succeed with zero warnings; commits are small with conventional messages, no em dashes, no AI attribution\u0022],\u0022Type\u0022:\u0022Feature\u0022,\u0022AgentContext\u0022:\u0022Brian\\u0027s direction on 2026-09-26 (relayed by run session odonomics-59): the walk should crawl every car the facets return, and the system, not he, visits them. This task is what makes an uncapped walk repeatable: without it, every rerun revisits every known car at about a minute a page. Evidence from walk run 5: carvana / Camry Hybrid states 149 cars, carvana / Corolla Hybrid 59, at roughly a minute per detail page. Code: src/Odonomics/Cli/Commands/WalkCommand.cs line 191 pulls anchors as [href, innerText] only, so card text needs a DOM-side change in that EvaluateAsync (walk up from each detail anchor to the ancestor whose innerText holds a dollar amount, or use a per-site selector); PageLink and SearchPageContent are the records it fills; WalkSite in src/Odonomics/Walk/WalkSites.cs holds the per-site patterns (DetailUrlPattern, SkippedCardTitlePattern, MatchCountPattern, ResultCardLinkPattern) and WalkSites.CanonicalDetailUrl canonicalizes a link; WalkSearchPages.CollectLinksAsync builds the pool; LedgerUpsertService.UpsertAsync (src/Odonomics/Ledger/LedgerUpsertService.cs) keys a posting on VIN, Source, and Url and stamps LastSeen with the run\\u0027s StartedAt, which LedgerDiffService relies on for Gone and Price drops, so a card touch that stamps LastSeen and appends a price observation slots into the existing diff with no diff change. Recorded card text: ~/Library/Application Support/Odonomics/walks/cars.com/20260926-121057/corolla-hybrid/search.txt lines 10 to 23 and walks/carvana/20260926-121057/corolla-hybrid/search.txt lines 88 to 94. A posting that was dropped on its detail visit (wrong model, new car) is not on the ledger and will be revisited; that is acceptable for now and out of scope. The Carvana shipping fee stays a detail-page fact; a card touch leaves the stored fee alone. the existing paging loop in WalkSearchPages.CollectLinksAsync then follows cars.com pages under the same stop rules as carvana (pool full, a page adding no new link, a No-exact-matches style marker if cars.com prints one); if the live site ignores page_size, the page=N loop alone still covers every result at the default page size; proven by URL-building tests and a CollectLinksAsync test with a fake loader returning three cars.com pages\u0022,\u0022Recorded file names stay unique when a cars.com pair has two searches and each is paged: the recorder names pages so search 1 page 2 and search 2 page 1 never collide (for example search-1-page-2.txt, or a scheme the README documents), and the console line names both the search and the page; the two searches still share the pair\\u0027s cap exactly as before; proven by a recorder-naming test\u0022,\u0022The README\\u0027s cars.com text (or docs/walk.md if the docs split has landed) says cars.com is paged like carvana and how the files are named; dotnet build and dotnet test succeed with zero warnings; commits are small with conventional messages, no em dashes, no AI attribution\u0022],\u0022Type\u0022:\u0022Feature\u0022,\u0022AgentContext\u0022:\u0022Brian\\u0027s direction on 2026-09-26 (relayed by run session odonomics-59): crawl every car the facets return. Evidence from walk run 5: cars.com / Camry Hybrid saved 30 from the first pages of its two searches with no paging, so the pair is truncated at page 1 whatever the cap. Code: src/Odonomics/Walk/WalkSites.cs lines 262 to 281 build the cars.com URL (stock_type, makes[], models[], zip, maximum_distance, year_min, mileage_max) with PagedSearchUrl left null; carvana\\u0027s PagedSearchUrl and the paging loop in src/Odonomics/Walk/WalkSearchPages.cs CollectLinksAsync are the precedent (PR #43, and PR #49 added the No-exact-matches stop and the stated-count bound); the recorder writes search.txt and search-2.txt for the two Camry searches today, so paging needs a naming scheme that does not collide. Verification status, stated plainly: the orchestrator could not confirm page and page_size against the live site this morning (a curl probe returned 403 and Brian\\u0027s browser was mid-walk); the names come from cars.com\\u0027s own pager and per-page selector (20, 50, 100). The run session will confirm in the browser after the walk; if page_size is rejected, drop it and keep page=N. The recorded cars.com search text carries no visible match count, so MatchCountPattern stays null unless a count is found on a recorded page.
